packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
packet-16 - unverified image reading (blind; no identification seen in context)

LAYOUT SURVEY (image-001.jpg, reduced overview)
- Two separate pieces of parchment photographed on black with colour checker and cm scale (scale reads ~3-38 cm).
- Upper piece: modern pencil "aus Hs 25" (number partly struck/overwritten?) and "Stams, STA, Fag. 8-1r". Landscape, ca. 18 x 14 cm. Surface heavily stained, offset/ghost marks (bluish, brownish) but no clearly legible script at overview scale; possibly a blank/flesh side or text almost completely erased. Sewing/nail holes along top edge and lower right; two burn-like holes lower left.
- Lower piece: pencil "aus Hs 25" (center) and "Stams, STA, Fag. 8-2r" (lower left). Ragged right and left edges; holes along top and bottom. Faint brown script visible in the upper middle-right: a block of short lines, several of which are longer at top (lines ~1-3 run across ca. 8-10 cm), then a narrow column of short line-beginnings (perhaps one word per line) running down to near the bottom. Text appears very faded/abraded. No rubrics, initials, or glosses identifiable at this scale.
- Interpretation (tentative): the lower piece may preserve the left-hand ends/beginnings of lines of a column whose remainder is lost or abraded, or a list-like text. Cannot tell orientation of text relative to the leaf without the tiles.

image-002.jpg (tile, upper-left of upper piece, Fag. 8-1r)
- No script visible. Grey/bluish smudge marks (offset or staining, roughly V-shaped) in upper middle; a faint horizontal line at ca. 55% height (possible fold/ruling? not certain). Tear at lower left. No letters, ruling with text, or erased writing I can discern. Nothing to transcribe.

image-003.jpg (tile, upper-right of upper piece, Fag. 8-1r; overlaps image-002 at the middle hole pair)
- No medieval script visible. Bluish stain at top centre. Along the right edge (ca. lines 780-1000 px) faint reddish-brown horizontal strokes, possibly offset or the very ends of ruled lines/letters; not resolvable into letters.
- Modern pencil, bottom: "aus Hs 25" (a stroke through the first digit-like mark before "25"; I read it as "#25" or "125" with the 1 struck; uncertain).
- Nothing medieval to transcribe.

image-004.jpg (tile, left side straddling both pieces: bottom of upper piece, top-left of lower piece)
- Upper piece (top half of tile): no script; two burn/rust holes. Nothing to transcribe.
- Lower piece (bottom of tile): a cursive documentary-looking hand (looped ascenders, brown ink, faded), not a formal book script. Only the left-hand starts of lines reach into this tile, at x ~ 750-1500 px; lines continue off right edge. Very abraded. Tentative:
  image-004 l.1 (y~1245): [illegible] q(?) p(ro)p(ter)(?) ... "c(?)a(?)u" [rest off tile]
  image-004 l.2 (y~1310): ...ui[illegible] [illegible]  ...ff [?]
  image-004 l.3 (y~1380): ...ce(?) u ... daz(?) / dat(?) ... "Gutem(?) / Gesten(?)" ... bl[?]
  image-004 l.4 (y~1445): ...tem(?) yat(?) / ...ten gut(?)
  image-004 l.5 (y~1505): ...[illegible]p(?)
  image-004 l.6 (y~1540): vn(?) / un(?) a(n)ttb(?)... (perhaps "vñ amtt..." ?)
  image-004 l.7 (y~1585): ...p(?) b(?)ezz(?)a ...
  image-004 l.8 (y~1640): ...amp(?)fang(?)...
  All of the above are guesses at letter shapes, not secure words. The script may be German (forms like "daz", "vñ" suggested) but this is uncertain. Better reading expected from tiles that centre on this text block.

image-005.jpg (tile, right side straddling both pieces; overlaps image-004 horizontally on the lower piece text)
- Upper piece: modern pencil "aus Hs [struck digit]25" and "Stams, STA, Frg. 8-1r" (I read "Frg." here rather than "Fag."). No medieval script.
- Lower piece: here the right ends of the text lines are visible; lines stop at x~1250-1300 px, well short of the parchment edge (x~1400), i.e. a right margin of ~2 cm survives with holes in it. So the text block on 8-2r sits in the upper-centre/right of the piece. Same faint cursive hand. Line-by-line (y positions on this tile); readings are letter-shape guesses, not secure:
  image-005 l.1 (y~1215): ...us  e/ (?)  ...  vrben(?)  d(er)  f[?]h[?]le(?)  ce[?]
  image-005 l.2 (y~1300): ...[illegible]  ze  Rh[?]e[?]bebuch[?]  [illegible]
  image-005 l.3 (y~1360): ...  [?]bal(?)  e  p(?)s(?)  ...  zelau[?]
  image-005 l.4 (y~1420): dez[?]y  vs(?)/v(?)frank(?)en(?)  hat
  image-005 l.5 (y~1485): ...y(?)  [illegible]  vñ  amth[?]
  image-005 l.6 (y~1545): Swer(?)/[?]wnd  [?]gast(?)  Besser(?)
  image-005 l.7 (y~1600): ... tob(?)  vn  vnferng(?)/vnsern(?) ...
- These line-ends should align with image-004 lines l.1-l.8 (same lines, image-004 shows their left parts). Alignment: image-005 l.4 "...hat" = image-004 l.4 "...ten gut(?)"/"...hal" region; image-005 l.5 "vñ amth" = image-004 l.6 "vn amttb"; so image-004 line numbering may be offset by one relative to image-005 from l.5 on. Uncertain.

image-006.jpg (tile, lower-left of lower piece, Fag. 8-2r; overlaps image-004 at top)
- Modern pencil: "aus Hs [struck]25" and "Stams, STA, Frg. 8-2r".
- Left two-thirds blank (stained). At right edge (x>1150) the left beginnings of text lines, overlapping image-004's lower lines at top, then continuing downward as a narrow strip of line-beginnings to y~1150. Readings (left starts only; lines cut by tile edge):
  image-006 l.1 (y~5): ...[illegible]  (overlap with image-004 l.3/4)
  image-006 l.2 (y~80): ...ki(?)  hat  [= image-004 l.5 "...hat"?]
  image-006 l.3 (y~135): [?]ffams(?) / Sstanc(?)  vn  amth[?]   [= image-004/005 "vn amtt"]
  image-006 l.4 (y~210): [?]r(?)  Bess[?]  ...  ff[?]   [= image-005 l.6 "Besser"]
  image-006 l.5 (y~290): ...  vnferng(?)[?]   [= image-005 l.7]
  image-006 l.6 (y~360): ...[?]z(?)  ...
  image-006 l.7 (y~440): Rv(?)ooo(?) / Rioos(?)
  image-006 l.8 (y~520): [?]  hat(?) / sum(?)
  image-006 l.9 (y~600): [?]erp(?)berg(?)
  image-006 l.10 (y~680): [?]...
  image-006 l.11 (y~760): ...(under pencil "aus Hs") [illegible]
  image-006 l.12 (y~830): ...ff(?) / [illegible]
  image-006 l.13 (y~920): z(?)
  image-006 l.14 (y~990): [?]ffes(?)/Messe(?)
  image-006 l.15 (y~1100): D(?)... [enlarged D-like initial or capital?]
- Interpretation (tentative): lower part looks like a list or column of short entries, each line starting at a similar left point; possibly a later addition/notes rather than a continuous text. Hand is very faded; these are not reliable readings.

image-007.jpg (tile, lower-right of lower piece, Fag. 8-2r; overlaps image-005 at top and image-006 at left)
- The best view of the text strip. Cursive hand, brown ink, looped b/h/l ascenders, long s/f descending below line. The narrow strip of line-beginnings sits at x~200-450 px; upper lines run further right (to x~700). Right of x~1000, between y~250 and ~1000 and again at the bottom, there are very faint ghost strokes, possibly an erased or abraded second block of text or offset; not legible.
- Lines (y on this tile). Same lines as image-005 l.4-l.7 and image-006 l.2-l.15:
  image-007 l.1 (y~45): [?]ey[?]en  vffzuck(?)en(?)  hat            [= image-005 l.4]
  image-007 l.2 (y~115): [?]ey[?]ewde(?)  vñ  amth[?]               [= image-005 l.5]
  image-007 l.3 (y~205): vnd(?)  [?]gast(?)/ vffgest(?)  Besse[?]   [= image-005 l.6]
  image-007 l.4 (y~290): z(?)  tod(?)  vñ  vnferng(?) / vnfeng(?) a[?]  [= image-005 l.7]
  image-007 l.5 (y~370): Gesp(?)ey  zwi(?)/ zeit(?)
  image-007 l.6 (y~450): Ilg(?) / Ag(?)  nowes(?)  [?]
  image-007 l.7 (y~525): gnen(?)  wat(?) / was(?)  [?]
  image-007 l.8 (y~600): vndgen(?) / vndeyn(?)
  image-007 l.9 (y~680): z  [?]vyde(?)    (stroke under pencil "25")
  image-007 l.10 (y~735): [?]ise(?)/ Ane(?) ...  (partly under pencil)
  image-007 l.11 (y~820): [?]fey(?) / e[?]ey
  image-007 l.12 (y~920): [?]  ee(?)
  image-007 l.13 (y~985): Cuoff(?)es / Chuffe(?)
  image-007 l.14 (y~1100): Dun(?) / Denn(?)  (enlarged D, perhaps a capital)
  image-007 l.15 (y~1160): ...[illegible faint]
  image-007 l.16 (y~1220): [illegible] ... [illegible]   (faint line running across to x~1000)
  image-007 l.17 (y~1290): [illegible]  ...  geb(?)  ...
  image-007 l.18 (y~1350): [?]ichob(?)/ gebß(?) ... [illegible]
  image-007 l.19 (y~1420): ...  dat(?) / dzit ... [illegible]
- Lower lines (l.15-19) run longer again and are extremely faint; holes interrupt them.
- Interpretation (tentative only): the language appears to be vernacular (German-looking: "vñ" = vnd, "hat", "vnd"), cursive. Layout of short single-word lines in the middle suggests verse-like short lines, a list, or a text whose right side has been lost/erased. I cannot settle which.

LAYOUT SURVEY, SECOND FACE (image-008.jpg, reduced overview)
- Same two pieces turned over: upper "Stams, STA, Frg. 8-1v" (pencil, upper left), lower "Stams, STA, Frg. 8-2v" (pencil, lower right). Held flat by glass/plastic weights.
- Both pieces carry long lines of German cursive (brown ink) running across the full width, cut at left and right edges (text lost at both sides), no columns, no rubrics or initials visible. Upper piece: ~18 lines, with a gap/blank region in the upper part (lines 1-5 partly, with stains) then ~12 dense lines. Lower piece: ~18-20 lines, much darker/stained, abraded, some text underlined near bottom ("...gegen..." line ~16).
- Tentative interpretation: a letter or documentary prose in German vernacular (words visible at overview: "vater", "frond", "sun"(?), "erben"). Pieces seem to be parts of the same sheet; the 8-2r side (strip of short lines) may be an address/endorsement or notes side. Not inferring further.

image-009.jpg (tile, upper-left of upper piece, Frg. 8-1v)
- German cursive (bastarda-like cursive, loops on d/b/h; long s; "y" used for final -n? e.g. "geſprochey"; I transcribe the y-shaped final as y). Left edge cut: line starts lost at the left on most lines. Large blank/stained area top centre. Lines (y on tile):
  image-009 l.1 (y~165): be wol n o[?]   [gap/hole]   vn deñ(?) / vn den
